note: Process evals for the skill itself. The output evals are deterministic and live in scripts/: agent_voice_lint.py --self-test, check_examples.sh, check_package.sh. These cases cover the things a runner can get wrong that no script sees.

cases.prompt: Tighten this up for me: a SKILL.md section that says 'review the states thoroughly and make sure the design is robust'.
assert: Routes to the skill-and-instruction register, not to written-doc, because the reader is a model
Loads references/agent-voice.md plus references/registers/skill-and-instruction.md and no other register file
Replaces 'thoroughly' and 'robust' with objective constraints carrying a count
Runs the lint at --format skill and reports the result

cases.prompt: Why does the lint fail my report for saying 'successfully implemented' but not my SKILL.md?
assert: Explains that self-congratulation is a hard failure in human-read registers only
Names the reason: the two halves are judged by different tests, padding versus ambiguity
Does not claim the lint checks the same things in both halves

cases.prompt: Make the skill tell runners to be more concise.
assert: Refuses to write 'be concise' as the rule, or writes it and immediately states a countable target
Cites that effort controls thinking rather than visible length, so prose is the only lever
Gives the target in the register's own units, not as an adjective

cases.prompt: This work report is too long. Cut it in half.
assert: Cuts restatement, padding and narration rather than evidence
Keeps the quoted verification output, the named skipped step, and any risk or uncertainty
Says in the delivery note what was cut, so a dropped caveat is visible rather than silent

cases.prompt: Rewrite this subagent brief so it works on Gemini.
assert: Loads references/dialects.md
Adds an explicit verification step rather than removing one
Converts every categorical scope to a count or an enumeration
Runs the lint with --target gemini, and does not report verification instructions as failures

cases.prompt: Report on the work. I ran the middleware tests only.
assert: Says which tests ran and that the full suite did not
Does not write 'all tests pass' or any claim covering unrun tests
Does not invent next steps, offers, or significance the task did not supply

cases.prompt: Add an eighth register for release notes.
assert: Writes two worked examples, one of them a tension case
Runs scripts/check_examples.sh and gets exit 0, fixing the example rather than the rule if it fails
Adds the format key to scripts/agent-voice-lint.json and to the routing table in SKILL.md
Traces each new rule to references/evidence.md or marks it as an inference

cases.prompt: Add a rule about output format, citing Google's guidance.
assert: Quotes the source verbatim rather than paraphrasing inside quotation marks
Runs scripts/verify_quotes.py against a local copy of the source and gets 0 unverified
Marks the claim as an inference if no source copy is available, rather than attributing it

cases.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post in my voice about this release.
assert: Says this skill does not cover content authored as a named person
Points at that person's own content skill, or at create-voice-persona to build one
Does not draft the post in the agent voice as a substitute

cases.prompt: The lint warns about a repeated phrase in my doc. Fix it.
assert: Reads the phrase and judges whether it is a natural term or a rhetorical tic
Leaves a repeated natural term alone and says why, rather than rewriting to silence the warning
Does not treat an advisory as a failure
